correctness.rationale: Each pair is a pseudo-intent because no singleton is nonclosed; any larger pseudo-intent must contain all projective lines between its members and hence would itself be closed. Full-support coefficients precisely characterize minimal independent rooted implications. Forced one-pass premises and a direct sufficiency argument yield the minimum grouped/unit counts; ordered independent point counting proves the product formula. The induction partitions each vector into two vectors supported on at most \(2^t\) original points, giving the exact support hierarchy. A full-support vector supplies the sharp rank-r lower bound. The standalone verifier recomputed exact spans, recursive pseudo-intents, minimal roots, counts, and rounds on PG(2,2), PG(2,3), and PG(3,2), with full subset checks on both projective planes. These are corroborating finite checks, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The size of a logical implication base versus its synchronous evaluation latency is a motivated knowledge-representation tradeoff. In a natural infinite family of finite projective closure lattices, exact formulas and the sharp rank-wise depth convert qualitative known basis theory into a quantitative size-versus-round hierarchy: a quadratic-in-ground-size canonical basis needs logarithmically many rounds, while the minimal one-pass basis has superpolynomial size in the number of ground points as dimension increases. This is a natural complete family-level invariant, not an isolated toy enumeration; scope is explicitly limited to projective span and synchronous semantics.
